# Abstract Security — AI working agreement

Shared context for every AI assistant in this workspace (Copilot, Cursor, Cline, Continue, Codex, Claude Code). Claude Code additionally loads the full system from `~/.claude`; the paths below are readable by any tool with filesystem access, so consult them rather than guessing.

## How to work here

- **State assumptions up front**; if a fact is unverified, say so — never present a guess as fact.
- **Evidence before completion**: run the command / read the file / check the output before claiming something works, is fixed, or is done. No "should work."
- **Surface risk early** — security, cost, data-loss, irreversible, or outward-facing actions get called out before I act.
- **Ground, don't guess** — for anything Abstract-specific (APIs, schemas, product, positioning, brand) follow the Grounding Protocol below.
- **Match the surrounding work** — code, prose, and design inherit the conventions already present.
- **Challenge & evolve (always on, every persona)** — don't just execute: question the ask and the status quo, propose better options, and actively look outward. Recommend better tools, new skills, connectors/MCPs, automations, schedulers, prompts, and workflows — researching how others (open-source projects, GitHub, Medium/blogs, forums, gists, competitors, vendor docs) solve the same problem across pipelines, aggregations, integrations, deployments, enrichments, parsers, mappers, detections, incidents, investigations, SOC automation, and AI workflows. Surface competitive comparisons and improvement/feedback loops. Invoke `abstract-challenger` for the research+recommendation playbook. Flag when a different approach would beat the requested one — with evidence.
- **Never quote a platform count — print it (added 2026-08-26).** Endpoint totals, action counts, deprecated counts, folder counts: every one of these has been wrong in at least one file at some point, and each stale number cost a re-derivation. The API inventory is `~/Documents/GitHub/Abstracts APIPhany/openapi/openapi.complete.json`, rebuilt by `refresh.sh --pull`, which ends by printing the counts. **Re-run it whenever a Linear ticket ships an endpoint, a parameter appears, a 500 turns into a 200, or you are about to state a number.** Read `x-abstract-source` / `verified` / `deprecated` provenance BEFORE calling an endpoint, and read the curated TRAP text in its description — it encodes a blocker that already cost a day. Full contract: `skills/abstract-knowledge/references/api-source-of-truth.md`.
- **"Fixed" means fixed everywhere in its class — prove it with `coverage-gate.py` (added 2026-09-06).** The most damaging failure of the Sequoia engagement was not a wrong diagnosis, it was a **true statement with an unstated scope**: "Front Door is fixed" meant *on two of four Event Hub configs*; "labels de-duplicated" meant *in one of six parser files*; "the Asset Directory joins at 49.7%" meant *against a global top-1000 aggregation, not the datasets it would enrich*. Each was verified where it was built and never enumerated across the population, so the same defect was rediscovered and re-diagnosed repeatedly and the customer lost confidence in every prior claim. **Before reporting any change as done: enumerate the full population it belongs to and show the count.** `dist/integrations-lab/bin/coverage-gate.py class --integration <substr>` lists every active config of a class with its parser files and dispatches and **exits 1 on drift**; `file --file <name>` asserts one file is present and byte-identical everywhere; `field --field <f> --datasets a,b,c` asserts a field is populated on every dataset. A config that legitimately cannot take the change is **named with its reason in the same breath**, never silently skipped. State scope in the sentence — "deployed to 3 of 4 configs; the 4th is a fork on `raw.*` and needs restoring first" — never a bare "done".
- **A zero is a claim, and it must be proven (added 2026-09-04).** An empty result is the most expensive lie this platform tells: it is indistinguishable from "found no problems", and it has now cost this practice detections that never fired, dashboards that read all-clear, and a customer's parser blamed for a defect it did not have. **Before charting, alerting or reporting on any field, prove it exists** with `POST /v1/kql/validate` (body `{"kql_query": "events | where <field> == \"x\""}`), which is first-party and answers against the tenant's real catalog: `unknown_field` means *"the search would silently match nothing"*, and it also names list fields, tokenized-text fields where `==` is a phrase match, and `ext.*` which is not KQL-searchable at all. A field can be VALID while the VALUE is wrong, so pair it with a coverage check. **Then distrust the zero itself** — field-analytics and StreamViewer both intermittently return a confident `total_count: 0` with `available: true` for data that is demonstrably present (measured: 4 empty in 10 identical calls). Retry three to five times and cross-check the other engine before reporting an absence. Never let an empty chart stand as evidence of nothing happening. Full detail: `skills/abstract-knowledge/references/api-source-of-truth.md`; memories `reference-kql-validate-field-gate`, `reference-abstract-silent-zero-queries`.
- **Capture the input, never author it — and read the mechanism before theorising (added 2026-09-13).** Three consecutive parser deploys regressed a live Sequoia feed in one session and **every one passed offline replay first**. The harness input was a fixture I hand-wrote, so it encoded my assumption about the record shape and the test confirmed that assumption instead of falsifying it. **A fabricated fixture cannot disprove the belief that produced it.** Three successive wrong mechanism theories (raw-is-an-object → raw-is-a-string → default.yml-does-the-promotion) all died once I read a REAL artifact instead of reasoning from code — `event.original` on an unparsed event, which holds the payload verbatim. (Note the adjacent trap, caught by testing the claim rather than assuming it: `GET /v2/pipelines/{id}/samples` shows the SOURCE PIPELINE's input — the parser's *output* — **not** the parser's input; a managed integration's samples are ACS-shaped too.) Rules, in order: (1) **fixtures are CAPTURED from production or the work does not proceed** — `dist/integrations-lab/bin/parser-ground-truth.py baseline <cfg>` before a change, `compare <before> <after>` after (exits 1 on any field ≥50% dropping >10pp); (2) **before any claim about how something works, read a real artifact** — the stored event or the pipeline sample, never the code alone; (3) **label every statement measured / inferred / guessed and never take a production write on "inferred"** — "this is a platform issue, escalate to engineering" was inferred from one negative result, stated as fact, and wrong; (4) **one production change per diagnosis** — after a failed deploy the next step is observation, not another build. Blast-radius guards (tenant pin, `--expect`, byte-verified rollback, smallest-feed canary) are **containment, not verification**: they limit the damage from a wrong belief, they never catch it. See `_ci/known-blockers.sh` **18** (one hard-failing processor discards the whole document — it presents as "the parser produced nothing") and **19** (never hand-write a fixture).
- **Declared is not deployed — and a 404 has THREE meanings (updated 2026-09-13).** `{"message":"Not found."}` is an API-gateway 404 — the route is in the spec but not shipped on that environment. `{"detail":"Not Found"}` is FastAPI — no such route. **A 404 carrying a SEMANTIC message** (e.g. `{"detail":"Agent configuration is not enabled"}`) means the route **EXISTS and a feature flag is off** — that third class is what made the whole v2 reports/widgets surface look unshipped when it is live on qa1. **A guessed id is not evidence:** substituting a harvested id into a path *or query* parameter turns "that id does not exist" into a 404 indistinguishable from "route missing" — this invented ten phantom endpoints in one session. **Trailing slashes are load-bearing** (`/v1/fleets` 307s, `/v1/fleets/` 200s), and a 405 proves nothing because a templated route swallows any literal — check the `Allow:` header on OPTIONS. **Never probe with DELETE against a production tenant.** Procedure before calling anything missing: probe qa1 → read `GET /v1/feature-flags/flags` → check the 404 body class → confirm no guessed id was involved. For non-prod spec pulls use `bin/env-spec-probe.sh`, never `refresh.sh --pull`, which would merge that environment's endpoints into the prod source of truth permanently.
- **A solved blocker must never be re-solved (standing).** Before diagnosing any platform oddity, run `_ci/known-blockers.sh list` and check the spec's TRAP descriptions. A newly-solved blocker gets encoded as a `known-blockers.sh` subcommand with a positive control — not as a paragraph someone has to remember to read.
- **Design intent is not a product** — the in-progress CS platform concept (its Command Center / Signals Queue / Hub building blocks) is design *intent* to drive vision only. **Never name or cite any WIP project/repo** (in outputs, docs, or to customers); treat it as anonymized possibility, and do real work through the live connectors + MCP.

## Non-negotiables

- **Ground, don't guess.** For anything Abstract-specific (APIs, schemas, product, brand) consult the reference files below. If a fact is unverified, say so — never present a guess as fact.
- **Evidence before completion.** Run the command, read the file, check the output before claiming something works. No "should work".
- **Secrets never touch the repo.** No tokens or keys in files that sync or get committed. Use the shell environment or the OS keychain.
- **Brand is exact.** Pink `#FF216B`, mid `#E8005D`, deep `#C2004C`, background `#060608`; accents teal `#01e69d`, amber `#f5c61e`, blue `#2e9bf0`. Fonts Barlow, Barlow Semi Condensed, JetBrains Mono. Use the official logo SVGs; never redraw the mark.
- **Customer-facing output carries no internal references** — no local paths, tenant identifiers, other customers, or internal tooling names.

## Multi-step workflows

Orchestration scripts. Claude Code runs them directly; other tools should read them to follow the same sequence.

| Workflow | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `aws-onboarding-launchpad` | Two-persona AWS onboarding: architecture decision → DevOps IaC pack → Security API create plan → validation gate |
| `competitive-teardown` | Competitive teardown of a named vendor: challenger fans out external research (parallel per axis), product-manager builds the analysis + feature matrix vs Abstract, and marketing turns it into displacement positioning. |
| `design-panel` | Convenes a customer-and-designers panel on a working deliverable whose STRUCTURE is wrong: each persona proposes one concrete layout/IA model, then a chief designer adjudicates them into a single implementable spec. |
| `experience-panel` | Runs a multi-persona experience review over any self-contained deliverable (an artifact, an app, a doc) and consolidates the findings into one ranked, de-duplicated ledger with an agreed fix list. |
| `gtm-launch` | End-to-end go-to-market pipeline for a feature/capability: product-manager writes the spec, marketing builds the messaging, designer produces launch assets, and writer authors the docs — each phase consuming the previous. |
| `integration-build` | Build an Abstract integration: research method → scaffold bundle + parser/mapper → validate |
| `integration-troubleshoot` | Diagnose a broken Abstract integration: gather evidence → symptom→check→fix → verify |
| `investigation-pipeline` | A natural-language threat investigation over the abstract-security MCP: translate the question to a ConditionGroup and search, enrich/interpret the hits, then (only when explicitly committed) record the finding as an insight and attach a timeline. |
| `log-review-to-detections` | Review a log sample → ACS fields → candidate detections + identity/asset models + MITRE + gaps |
| `onboarding-pipeline` | Post-sale onboarding handoff for a new account: sales-engineer packages the technical-win context, enablement builds the onboarding plan (kickoff + 30/60/90 + training), and the customer-success-architect turns it into a concrete deployment plan. |
| `qbr-builder` | Builds a Quarterly Business Review for one account: revops computes the metrics pack (from Notion CS Command Center + live MCP telemetry), CSM/CSA write the narrative, and designer produces a brand-exact deck. |
| `session-harvest` | Mine local Claude Code sessions for durable Abstract integration/OTEL/detection lessons |
| `tenant-health-check` | Composes a tenant health summary from the abstract-security MCP — there is no single health tool, so it gathers insights, event volume/trend, and a timeline in parallel per tenant, then synthesizes a graded health read. |
| `vendor-research` | Research one vendor across collection methods; rank by data richness; recommend integration(s) |

Source: `/Users/mherbert/.claude/workflows`
